questions.text: An entity leases a specialized machine and controls its use for several years, although legal title remains with the lessor. Which principle is most relevant in assessing whether an asset exists?

options.a: A plan to purchase equipment during the following fiscal year.
options.b: Receipt of cash before any productive resource is recognized.
options.c: Legal ownership regardless of access to economic benefits.
options.d: The mere intention to control a resource next year is sufficient for asset recognition, even without any past transaction or event.
options.e: Only legal ownership at the reporting date permits recognition; operating control is relevant solely for disclosure.
options.f: Control of future economic benefits resulting from a past event.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Accounts receivable are reported net of estimated uncollectible amounts.
II. Cash equivalents normally have a very short original maturity.
III. Prepaid insurance is always reported as a current liability.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: None of I, II or III
options.d: I, II and III

questions.text: A retailer holds €150m cash, has annual sales of €4,000m and applies the lecture's 1%-of-sales operating-cash rule. How much is classified as excess cash under this rule?
Assume inventory purchase prices rise throughout a period, inventory quantities are stable, and the same physical goods are sold. Relative to LIFO, FIFO generally produces:

options.a: higher COGS and higher net income, because the oldest purchase layers determine the income statement.
options.b: higher gross profit but lower inventory, because cost layers are assigned to sales first.
options.c: lower COGS and lower reported ending inventory.
options.d: higher COGS and lower reported ending inventory.
options.e: higher COGS and higher reported ending inventory.
options.f: lower COGS and higher reported ending inventory.

questions.text: A firm uses IFRS and proposes switching from weighted average inventory accounting to LIFO to reduce taxable income during inflation. Which assessment is accurate?

options.a: LIFO is permitted under IFRS if the tax authority accepts the inventory values.
options.b: LIFO is permitted if the company discloses its effect and applies the policy to all inventory.
options.c: LIFO is prohibited under IFRS, regardless of its potential earnings effect.
options.d: LIFO is required when prices rise, because it minimizes the chance of overstating profits.
options.e: LIFO is permitted under IFRS only if FIFO would raise inventory turnover.
options.f: LIFO is required under IFRS whenever inventories increase in value.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. FIFO usually leaves more recently acquired costs in inventory.
II. Under rising prices, FIFO will generally produce lower net income than LIFO.
III. Weighted average smooths the effect of different inventory purchase costs.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.b: I and II only
options.c: II only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A manufacturer reports COGS of €720m, inventory of €130m at the beginning and €110m at the end of the year. What are inventory turnover and DIO (365-day basis)?

options.a: 6.00 times and 60.83 days
options.b: 5.54 times and 65.90 days
options.c: 6.55 times and 55.76 days
options.d: 6.00 times and 50.00 days

questions.text: A company's DIO increases while prices and sales remain broadly stable. Which explanation requires the least additional assumptions?

options.a: Customers now pay their outstanding invoices faster than in previous years.
options.b: The company has reduced operating capital because inventories remain unsold.
options.c: Product quality has definitely risen because the firm carries more inventory.
options.d: Inventory is held longer on average; quality or production efficiency should be investigated.

questions.text: A company reduces DIO from 65 days to 53 days while annual COGS is €730m. Holding other factors constant, the approximate working-capital cash impact is:

options.a: €36m cash absorbed
options.b: €12m cash released
options.c: €24m cash absorbed
options.d: €24m cash released

questions.text: Which operational measure most directly targets an accumulation of work-in-process inventory?

options.a: Increasing finished-goods safety stock to keep all production stages fully utilized regardless of customer demand.
options.b: Reclassifying held inventory as a long-term intangible asset.
options.c: Increasing credit terms offered to wholesale customers.
options.d: Increasing work-in-process buffers at bottlenecks necessarily reduces inventory holding time and eliminates the need to match production to demand.
options.e: Removing production bottlenecks through improved manufacturing flow.
options.f: Refinancing long-term bonds at lower fixed interest rates.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Higher DIO always improves liquidity, irrespective of profitability.
II. Just-in-time deliveries can lower raw-material holding costs.
III. Demand-pull production responds to actual customer demand.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.b: None of I, II or III
options.c: I and II only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: Sales rise by 5% while average receivables rise by 20%. What happens to receivables turnover, all else equal?

options.a: It increases, suggesting customers are paying more rapidly.
options.b: It is unchanged, because receivables and revenue both rise.
options.c: It decreases, suggesting cash collection is becoming slower.
options.d: It becomes negative, because credit sales increase more slowly.

questions.text: A company reports annual sales of €1,095m and average trade receivables of €90m. What DSO does the lecture's formula imply?

options.a: 45 days
options.b: 33 days
options.c: 25 days
options.d: 27 days

questions.text: An aging analysis finds that invoices outstanding for over 120 days doubled, but total credit sales were flat. Which adjustment is most directly justified?

options.a: Increase the historical purchase cost of merchandise inventory.
options.b: Reassess the allowance for expected uncollectible receivables.
options.c: Recognize the future collection of overdue invoices as current sales.
options.d: Reverse all depreciation recorded on property and equipment.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Rising accounts receivable as a percentage of sales always improves cash generation.
II. Rising DSO can be a warning sign of deteriorating credit quality.
III. Declining receivables turnover may reflect more permissive customer credit terms.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I, II and III
options.b: II and III only
options.c: I only
options.d: I and III only

questions.text: A capital-intensive firm increases annual sales from €900m to €990m while average PPE increases from €300m to €360m. What happens to its PPE turnover?

options.a: It rises from 3.00 to 3.30, since a 10% increase in sales must improve turnover even if average PPE rises by 20%.
options.b: It rises from 2.75 to 3.00, because the denominator is based on ending assets only.
options.c: It falls from 3.00 to 2.75, suggesting weaker asset utilization.
options.d: It rises from 2.75 to 3.00, suggesting unchanged asset utilization.
options.e: It falls from 3.33 to 2.75, suggesting improved asset utilization.
options.f: It rises from 3.00 to 3.30, suggesting stronger asset utilization.

questions.text: A manufacturer has average depreciable asset cost of €1,800m and annual straight-line depreciation of €90m, with zero salvage value assumed. The implied average useful life is:

options.a: 20 years
options.b: 25 years
options.c: 18 years
options.d: 15 years

questions.text: Why does the lecture exclude land and construction-in-progress when estimating average useful life of depreciable PPE?

options.a: Those categories must be expensed before any assets can be capitalized.
options.b: Those categories are always financed by shareholders rather than creditors.
options.c: Those categories are generally not depreciated in the same way as assets in use.
options.d: Those categories are excluded from every measure of the firm's total assets.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Percent used up measures the market value of a firm's depreciable equipment.
II. High percent used up can signal substantial future replacement investment.
III. Percent used up compares accumulated depreciation with depreciable asset cost.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II and III only
options.b: I and II only
options.c: I, II and III
options.d: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A firm reports accumulated depreciation of €840m and average gross depreciable assets of €1,200m. If there have been no major revaluations, its percent used up is:
Two otherwise comparable manufacturers report PPE turnover of 4.0 and 2.0. Which interpretation follows most directly?

options.a: The second necessarily has a younger production asset base and lower maintenance needs.
options.b: The second generates more sales per euro of average PPE, holding utilization constant.
options.c: The first necessarily has the lower total depreciation expense because higher PPE turnover implies younger equipment.
options.d: The first reports twice as much operating cash, regardless of its payment terms.
options.e: The first generates more sales per euro of average PPE, although business mix still matters.

questions.text: A firm creates a brand organically through many years of advertising; another buys a similar trademark in an acquisition. Which recognition difference is most consistent with the chapter?

options.a: The acquired identifiable trademark may be capitalized while the internally built brand is often absent.
options.b: Both brands must be treated as goodwill, regardless of whether they were separately identified.
options.c: The internally built brand must also be capitalized because similar acquired trademarks have an observable market price.
options.d: The internally built brand must be capitalized while the acquired trademark is always expensed.
options.e: Neither brand can ever be recognized because trademarks have no physical substance.
options.f: Both internally generated and acquired brands are recognized at the same estimated market value when management can demonstrate profitability.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Goodwill is routinely amortized over a fixed useful life under IFRS.
II. Indefinite-lived intangible assets are tested for impairment annually.
III. Finite-lived purchased intangible assets are generally amortized.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II and III only
options.b: I, II and III
options.c: II only
options.d: I and II only
options.e: None of I, II or III

questions.text: A company pays €520m for a business whose separately identifiable assets are fair-valued at €470m and liabilities at €130m. Goodwill recognized at acquisition is:
An acquisition includes identifiable customer contracts, patented technology and the assembled workforce. Which concept is most appropriate for amounts not assigned to identifiable net assets?

options.a: Residual goodwill arising from the business combination.
options.b: Any unallocated consideration must be recorded as cash retained by the acquired firm rather than an intangible asset.
options.c: A reduction in purchased PP&E equal to all future earnings.
options.d: An immediate dividend to the acquirer's existing shareholders.
options.e: The residual consideration must be allocated entirely to the assembled workforce as a separately identifiable intangible asset.
options.f: A deferred revenue liability for every intangible capability.

questions.text: When management writes down goodwill after an impairment test, which pair of financial statements is affected most directly?

options.a: The income statement records a loss, and the balance sheet shows lower goodwill.
options.b: The equity statement records new shares, and the income statement records higher revenue.
options.c: The cash-flow statement records a cash outflow, and the balance sheet shows higher goodwill.
options.d: The balance sheet records higher receivables, and the income statement records a gain.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. An unexpected deterioration of a cash-generating unit can trigger additional testing.
II. Impairment losses generally produce an equal-period cash payment to creditors.
III. Goodwill impairment testing is required annually.
Which set is correct?

options.a: II and III only
options.b: I and II only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: III only

questions.text: A retailer holds 30% of its assets as purchased goodwill, whereas a competitor holds 4%. Which next step is most informative?

options.a: Conclude that the first retailer's acquisition synergies have already been realized in cash.
options.b: Infer that the second retailer has recorded all valuable intangible assets at market value.
options.c: Investigate acquisition history and whether projected cash flows support goodwill recoverability.
options.d: Conclude that the first retailer necessarily has a higher sustainable competitive advantage.

questions.text: An investment purchased with an original maturity of 150 days has 25 days remaining until maturity. Under the lecture's cash-equivalent convention, it is generally:

options.a: a cash equivalent because its remaining maturity is below 90 days.
options.b: an operating receivable because its remaining maturity is below one year.
options.c: an inventory item because it will be converted into cash before year-end.
options.d: not a cash equivalent solely because its remaining maturity is short.
options.e: necessarily a non-current asset because its original maturity exceeded 90 days, even when its settlement is due within a year.
options.f: automatically cash and cash equivalents because it will be repaid within 30 days.

questions.text: Which is a valid reason that a high PPE-turnover firm may not be more operationally efficient than a low PPE-turnover firm?

options.a: The ratio includes dividends and thus primarily reflects shareholder financing.
options.b: A high turnover ratio always results from recording a larger depreciation expense.
options.c: PPE turnover is independent of sales and therefore cannot indicate asset utilization.
options.d: The firms may operate in industries requiring very different production technologies.

questions.text: A firm's inventory turnover improves from 4.0 to 5.0, while DSO worsens from 35 to 47 days. Which statement is correct?

options.a: Its DIO rises by 12 days, while improved customer credit cancels that deterioration.
options.b: Its DIO falls by 12 days, and slower collection exactly offsets the inventory benefit.
options.c: Its DIO decreases by 12.0 days, entirely neutralizing the 12-day deterioration in collection.
options.d: Its DIO falls by 18.25 days, but slower collection offsets part of the cash benefit.
options.e: Its DIO increases by 18.25 days, so CCC necessarily increases even if payables are unchanged.
options.f: Its DIO rises by 18.25 days, and slower collection reinforces the cash benefit.

questions.text: Which change would reduce reported accounts receivable net of allowances without any new customer payments?

options.a: An extension of the credit terms granted on existing invoices.
options.b: An increase in the estimated allowance for uncollectible accounts.
options.c: A reclassification of short-term deposits into cash equivalents.
options.d: An increase in the invoice amount issued to a credit customer.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. An increase in PPE turnover necessarily proves a rise in the market value of PPE.
II. A decrease in inventory turnover generally increases DIO.
III. An increase in DSO can stem from a more generous credit policy.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and III only
options.b: II only
options.c: I, II and III
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A company's inventory is valued under FIFO in a period of sharply falling purchase prices. Relative to LIFO (hypothetically), FIFO will typically report:

options.a: higher COGS and lower closing inventory, assuming inventory quantities are stable.
options.b: higher COGS and higher closing inventory, assuming inventory quantities are stable.
options.c: lower COGS and higher closing inventory, assuming inventory quantities are stable.
options.d: lower COGS and lower closing inventory, assuming inventory quantities are stable.

questions.text: A firm has €240m net PPE and €60m intangible assets. Its total assets are €1,000m. Another firm has the same amounts but total assets of €600m. What does common-size analysis reveal?

options.a: The first company has the higher percentage of assets allocated to PPE and intangibles because its total assets are larger.
options.b: The first allocates 24% and the second 40%, because intangible assets are excluded from the comparison.
options.c: Both allocate 30% of assets because their book amounts match exactly.
options.d: The first allocates 50% of assets to these items; the second allocates 30%.
options.e: The first allocates 30% of assets to these items; the second allocates 50%.
options.f: Both allocate 50% of assets because common-size analysis uses equal totals.

questions.text: An analyst observes steadily declining PPE turnover and rising percent used up. Which paired concern is most justified?

options.a: Lower cost of goods sold per unit alongside a proven increase in residual asset values.
options.b: Less revenue per euro of PPE alongside a potentially aging and less efficient asset base.
options.c: More revenue per euro of PPE alongside evidence of lower replacement spending requirements.
options.d: Faster collection of receivables alongside evidence of an improving inventory mix.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. Goodwill is recognized as a residual in a business combination.
II. A standalone purchase of a patented technology must always create goodwill.
III. An indefinite useful life does not imply freedom from impairment testing.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I and II only
options.b: II only
options.c: I and III only
options.d: II and III only

questions.text: A supermarket reduces its inventory balance without changing purchase volumes, sales volume or payment policy. Which transaction could explain a lower closing balance?

options.a: An equity share issue that raises cash but leaves merchandise unchanged.
options.b: An ordinary repayment of long-term debt using existing cash deposits.
options.c: A management decision to extend receivables terms to wholesalers.
options.d: A change in inventory carrying cost assumptions or a write-down to recoverable value.

questions.text: A firm reduces DSO by 10 days at annual sales of €1,825m. Under the lecture's simplified cash-impact reasoning, approximately how much cash is released?
Which condition most weakens the interpretation that a falling DIO unequivocally indicates better inventory management?

options.a: The elimination of production bottlenecks that lower work-in-process inventories.
options.b: The reduction of storage costs through more reliable raw-material deliveries.
options.c: A stockout-driven fall in inventory that disrupts profitable customer deliveries.
options.d: A decline in average inventory because of better sales forecasting accuracy.

questions.text: A firm acquired a competitor for €900m, recognizing €240m goodwill. Two years later the acquired unit loses a major customer. Which response best reflects the financial reporting implications?

options.a: Reassess recoverability of the unit and recognize an impairment if carrying value is unsupported.
options.b: Amortize the goodwill by €120m each year because every business has a two-year life.
options.c: Recognize an offsetting increase in contributed capital to preserve reported net assets.
options.d: Transfer all goodwill to cash equivalents to avoid operating-income volatility.

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. All intangible assets have physical substance.
II. Acquired goodwill is amortized annually under IFRS.
III. An asset can exist without legal ownership if the company controls the benefits.
Which set is correct?

options.a: III only
options.b: I only
options.c: II only
options.d: None of I, II or III

questions.text:
Consider the statements.
I. DIO decreases when inventory turnover increases, holding the day count fixed.
II. Purchased finite-lived intangibles are normally subject to amortization.
III. A rising receivables-to-sales ratio can flag deteriorating collections.
Which set is correct?

options.a: I only
options.b: II and III only
options.c: I, II and III
options.d: I and III only
